title: Choose the tools, then debug the whole application
outcome: Explain a production tool map and recover a synthetic incident without adding every tool by default.
useCase: An end-of-course tool selection and incident exercise.
benefits: Connects tools to responsibilities and practical diagnosis.
drawbacks: A reference architecture is not a requirement to deploy every part.
version: Pinned local examples · version-labelled configuration fragments
cue: Choose fewer tools well. Trace one item completely.

trace.title: Requirement and tool role
trace.detail: A production architecture is a set of responsibilities. Packaging, orchestration, storage, messaging, observation, delivery, scheduling, and product analytics are different jobs. Several products can cover overlapping parts. Choose a coherent minimum and justify each additional tool.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Begin at user impact. Identify the authority and each queued/retained copy. Find the oldest uncompleted item and its event/run ID. Distinguish delivery, processing, and UI problems. Repair the smallest broken boundary and verify both backlog recovery and user-visible completion.

Finish the cumulative toolkit quiz, then explain why a plausible alternative tool is a poor fit for three scenarios. Selection reasoning matters more than logo recognition.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Adding capacity to a poison-message loop can worsen the DB incident. Installing every monitoring stack can duplicate cost without improving a question. Product analytics cannot substitute for a durable business audit trail.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Explain a production tool map and recover a synthetic incident without adding every tool by default. Explain one example and one failure.
